r0.why: Extremely vesicular rough volcanic glass, crystals optional, pumicite as powder [1]; light-colored [2]; igneous and foamy [44]; pumex and spuma [45].

r1.why: Super-heated pressurized rock ejected rapidly [4]; simultaneous cooling and depressurization [5]; lower gas solubility makes gases exsolve, carbonated drink comparison [6]; bubbles frozen [7].

r2.why: Porosity 64-85%, floats possibly for years until waterlogged [16]; rafts hazard to ships [9]; Krakatoa rafts up to 20 years with tree trunks [29]; Tonga to Fiji [31]; marine species [30].

r3.why: Pale, colour range, black from scattered magnetite crystals [12]; confusion with black scoria [13]; commonly silicic/felsic to intermediate, never mafic [11].

r4.why: Two main vesicle forms [18]; tubular microvesicles giving silky or fibrous fabric [19]; spherical ones from high vapor pressure [21]; tube/woody pumice resembling wood [22][23][24]; 'bubbles' is only a plain gloss of vesicles.

r5.why: Scoria vesicular, larger vesicles, thicker walls, dark and denser [3][35]; often sinks but not always [36]; difference from lower magma viscosity [38].
